name: Compare & Contrast
description: Two or three easily confused things set side by side: definitions, a comparison table, where they overlap, a misconception, and a check.
audience: Teaching differences: mitosis vs meiosis, simple vs compound interest, plant vs animal cells.

signals.why: your words ask for a comparison
the topic is two things to tell apart

slides.guidance: Lesson title for {topic} and a short subtitle that names the class level.
Students will be able to tell {topic} apart and explain how.
Define the first of the things being compared in {topic}, in one plain sentence.
Compare the things in {topic} on the attributes students most confuse. Exactly the things named in the topic.
What the things in {topic} have in common, and where they genuinely differ.
The most common mix-up between the things in {topic}, and how to remember the difference.

variants.guidance: A classroom meme about {topic}. Pick one format from MEME FORMATS that matches the idea, write captions a {grade} student finds funny and that make the correct idea easier to remember. Kind to students, never about a person.

slides.guidance: A question where the options are the things being compared, to check students can tell them apart.
One line per thing, then the single difference that matters most.
